1	# PROGRAM.md — the live research program
2	
3	This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
4	Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
5	it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
6	`experiments/` and `novel/`.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
11	π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.
12	
13	**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
14	approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
15	theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
16	GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
17	mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
18	honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
19	with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
20	adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.
21	
22	## ACTIVE LINE — the verification program (started S491, 2026-06-13)

# PROGRAM.md — the live research program

This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
`experiments/` and `novel/`.

## Goal

An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.

**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.

## ACTIVE LINE — the verification program (started S491, 2026-06-13)

3	certificate_profile.py -- S509.  Characterize the FULL non-interactive certificate
4	for "pi(x) = c" and LOCATE the Õ(sqrt x) communication wall.
5	
6	CONTEXT.  By S508 the whole-chain VERIFIER's expensive sub-term -- the count of
7	large-table (mle_eval over a sqrt-x-size cube) evaluations -- is Õ(x^{1/4}) (the
8	two S_0 base closes go through the tensor PCS; every per-layer leaf open was
9	removed by pcs+batch_trace+batch_ub).  The verifier side of the milestone is met.
10	The quantity that is STILL Õ(sqrt x) is the certificate SIZE itself: stats["comm"]
11	(the Fiat-Shamir transcript) has slope ~0.5 in every config.  This file pins down
12	exactly WHERE that Õ(sqrt x) lives.
13	
14	WHAT IS MEASURED (full succinct config = delegate+structured+pcs+batch_trace+
15	batch_ub+batch_wiring+commit_base, over n in {8..18}):
16	  (i)   certificate SIZE = total stats["comm"] in field elements AND in bits
17	        (bits = elems * ceil(log2 q); BIG_Q elems are 61-bit, Q elems 31-bit --
18	        a constant factor, same exponent);
19	  (ii)  verifier op-count = vleaf_ops_pl + vleaf_ops_ot (== vcommit_ops in this
20	        config -- the only LARGE-table work left is the one-time PCS base opens);
21	  (iii) prover wall.
22	Each exponent is fitted (alpha = d log2(metric) / d n, so alpha~1 => Theta(x),
23	alpha~0.5 => Theta(sqrt x), alpha~0.25 => Theta(x^{1/4})).
24	
25	The full config STRICTLY EXTENDS the S508 "config (d)" named in PROGRAM.md by also
26	turning on batch_wiring (built S503/S504 precisely to cut comm ~5x): with the
27	wiring batched, comm_outer is PURELY the sequential two-sided layer reductions, the
28	cleanest form of the result.  We also print the no-batch_wiring variant to show the
29	conclusion is robust either way (there the batchable wiring is merely folded into
30	comm_outer, making it even more dominant).
31	
32	ATTRIBUTION.  run_chain (S509) partitions stats["comm"] by source -- a purely
33	additive boundary-snapshot, transcript unchanged:
34	  comm_outer : the K = pi(sqrt x) SEQUENTIAL per-layer two-sided reductions
35	               (phase-A/phase-B outer sum-checks + the pcs line/claim folds).
36	  comm_bt    : the ONE batched trace zero-test (all K layers).
37	  comm_bw    : the ONE batched wiring discharge (all 2K-1 wirings).
38	  comm_ub    : the ONE batched Ub-opening discharge (all K*nb leaves).
39	  comm_base  : the two one-time S_0 closes (tensor-PCS eval proofs).
40	The five sum EXACTLY to stats["comm"] (asserted).
41	
42	HEADLINE RESULT.  The Õ(sqrt x) certificate is DOMINATED by comm_outer (60% -> 90%
43	of the total as n: 8 -> 18, and -> 100% asymptotically): after EVERY batchable
44	obligation has been batched (trace/wiring/Ub -> polylog) and the base committed
45	(-> x^{1/4}), the only term left at Theta(sqrt x) is the K sequential layer
46	reductions.  comm_outer ~ K * nb^2 = pi(sqrt x) * O(log^2 x) = Theta(sqrt x polylog).
47	
48	MEMBERSHIP STATEMENT this yields.  L_pi = {(x,c) : pi(x) = c} has, under a
49	collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle assumption (Fiat-Shamir of the chain), a
50	NON-INTERACTIVE certificate of size Õ(sqrt x) field elements (Õ(sqrt x * log^2 x)
51	bits), whose expensive (large-table) verifier work is Õ(x^{1/4}).  HONEST: the
52	verifier must READ the Õ(sqrt x) proof (each transcript scalar is an O(1) sum-check
53	round check), so TOTAL verification is Theta(sqrt x) -- bounded below by the proof
54	size.  The Õ(x^{1/4}) of S508 is the large-table-eval SUB-term only; this file makes
55	that explicit.  Compressing the SIZE (and hence total verification) below sqrt x to
56	polylog requires batching the K SEQUENTIAL outer reductions -- which hits the SAME
57	wall as open item 2 (the layer-batching closed negative): each layer's OUTPUT claim
58	is the next layer's INPUT claim, a dependency chain, unlike the trace/Ub/wiring
59	obligations (independent per-layer witnesses sharing one random trajectory, hence
60	batchable).  The semigroup generated by v |-> floor(v/p) is the precise obstruction.
61	
62	FALSIFIERS (any one would break the result):
63	  * total comm exponent NOT ~0.5 (we assert it lands in [0.4, 0.65]);
64	  * the per-source attribution NOT summing to the measured comm (asserted exactly);
65	  * comm_outer NOT the dominant / growing fraction, or its exponent NOT ~0.5;
66	  * the batched-discharge / base exponents NOT sub-0.5 (they should be polylog or
67	    x^{1/4});
68	  * verifier-op exponent NOT ~0.25 (re-confirms S508);
69	  * claimed pi(x) differing from the sieve in any config / field;
70	  * a claimed batching of the SEQUENTIAL outer reductions that actually drops the
71	    comm exponent below 0.5 -- that would be a genuine breakthrough (it batches the
72	    floor(v/p) semigroup), NOT a measurement; verify it against open item 2 before
73	    believing it.
74	
75	CLI:
76	  python3 certificate_profile.py --selftest
77	  python3 certificate_profile.py                 # the profile (default q, n=8..18)
78	  python3 certificate_profile.py --field big     # over BIG_Q=2^61-1 (61-bit elems)
79	"""
80	import argparse
81	import math
82	import time
83	
84	import numpy as np
85	
86	import compressed_layer as cl
87	
88	# the minimal certificate: every batchable obligation batched, base committed.
89	FULL = dict(delegate=True, structured=True, pcs=True, batch_trace=True,
90	            batch_ub=True, batch_wiring=True, commit_base=True)
91	# the literal S508 "config (d)" -- wiring NOT batched (discharged inline per layer).
92	NOBW = dict(delegate=True, structured=True, pcs=True, batch_trace=True,
93	            batch_ub=True, commit_base=True)
94	
95	COMM_SRCS = ["comm_outer", "comm_bt", "comm_bw", "comm_ub", "comm_base"]
96	FIELDS = {"q": cl.Q, "big": cl.BIG_Q}
97	
98	
99	def _verifier_ops(r):
100	    """Large-table (mle_eval / PCS) field-op count -- the S507/S508 metric."""
101	    return r["vleaf_ops_pl"] + r["vleaf_ops_ot"]
102	
103	
104	def measure(ns, cfg, q, seed=1, check_truth=True):
105	    """Run run_chain over ns with cfg; return {n: result} (result carries an
106	    added 'wall' and 'x').  Asserts accept, claimed==sieve, and that the comm
107	    attribution sums exactly to stats['comm']."""
108	    out = {}
109	    for n in ns:
110	        x = (1 << n) - 1
111	        t = time.perf_counter()
112	        r = cl.run_chain(x, np.random.default_rng(seed), q=q, **cfg)
113	        r["wall"] = time.perf_counter() - t
114	        r["x"] = x
115	        if check_truth:
116	            assert r["accepted"], (n, "rejected honest run")
117	            assert r["claimed"] == cl.sieve_pi(x), (n, r["claimed"])
118	        # attribution closes exactly
119	        parts = sum(r[k] for k in COMM_SRCS)
120	        assert parts == r["comm"], (n, "comm attribution gap", parts, r["comm"])
121	        out[n] = r
122	    return out
123	
124	
125	def _fit(ns, vals):
126	    return cl._fit_slope(list(ns), [math.log2(max(1, v)) for v in vals])
127	
128	
129	def profile(ns=(8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18), field="q", seed=1):
130	    q = FIELDS[field]
131	    bpe = q.bit_length()                       # bits per field element (31 / 61)
132	    print(f"=== certificate profile (full succinct config), field={field} "
133	          f"({bpe}-bit elems) ===")
134	    print("config = delegate+structured+pcs+batch_trace+batch_ub+batch_wiring"
135	          "+commit_base")
136	    data = measure(ns, FULL, q, seed)
137	
138	    # ---- table 1: size / verifier ops / prover wall ----
139	    print("\n-- certificate SIZE, VERIFIER ops, PROVER wall --")
140	    print(f"{'n':>3} {'x':>9} {'V':>6} {'nb':>3} {'K':>4} {'pi':>7} | "
141	          f"{'cert_elems':>10} {'cert_KB':>8} | {'verif_ops':>9} | "
142	          f"{'prover_s':>8}")
143	    for n in ns:
144	        r = data[n]
145	        x = r["x"]; V = cl.isqrt(x); nb = max(1, V.bit_length()); K = r["layers"]
146	        kb = r["comm"] * bpe / 8 / 1024
147	        print(f"{n:>3} {x:>9} {V:>6} {nb:>3} {K:>4} {r['claimed']:>7} | "
148	              f"{r['comm']:>10} {kb:>8.2f} | {_verifier_ops(r):>9} | "
149	              f"{r['wall']:>8.3f}")
150	
151	    # ---- table 2: per-source comm attribution ----
152	    print("\n-- comm ATTRIBUTION by source (field elements; outer = the K "
153	          "sequential layer reductions) --")
154	    print(f"{'n':>3} {'comm':>8} | {'outer':>8} {'out%':>5} | {'bt':>5} "
155	          f"{'bw':>6} {'ub':>5} {'base':>6}")
156	    for n in ns:
157	        r = data[n]
158	        pct = 100.0 * r["comm_outer"] / r["comm"]
159	        print(f"{n:>3} {r['comm']:>8} | {r['comm_outer']:>8} {pct:>4.0f}% | "
160	              f"{r['comm_bt']:>5} {r['comm_bw']:>6} {r['comm_ub']:>5} "
161	              f"{r['comm_base']:>6}")
162	
163	    # ---- table 3: effect of batching the wiring (full vs S508 config (d)) ----
164	    print("\n-- comm: full (wiring batched) vs S508 config (d) (wiring inline) --")
165	    dnobw = measure(ns, NOBW, q, seed)
166	    print(f"{'n':>3} {'full_comm':>9} {'full_outer':>11} || "
167	          f"{'d_comm':>8} {'d_outer':>8}  (inline wiring folds into outer)")
168	    for n in ns:
169	        print(f"{n:>3} {data[n]['comm']:>9} {data[n]['comm_outer']:>11} || "
170	              f"{dnobw[n]['comm']:>8} {dnobw[n]['comm_outer']:>8}")
171	
172	    # ---- exponent fits ----
173	    last = ns[-4:]
174	    print(f"\n-- fitted exponents alpha (metric ~ x^alpha; log2(metric) vs n, "
175	          f"last {len(last)} pts: n in {tuple(last)}) --")
176	    fits = {}
177	    rows = [
178	        ("comm (cert size)", [data[n]["comm"] for n in last], "~0.5  Theta(sqrt x)"),
179	        ("  comm_outer",     [data[n]["comm_outer"] for n in last], "~0.5  Theta(sqrt x)  <-- DOMINANT"),
180	        ("  comm_bt",        [data[n]["comm_bt"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
181	        ("  comm_bw",        [data[n]["comm_bw"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
182	        ("  comm_ub",        [data[n]["comm_ub"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
183	        ("  comm_base",      [data[n]["comm_base"] for n in last], "~0.25 Theta(x^1/4) PCS"),
184	        ("verifier ops",     [_verifier_ops(data[n]) for n in last], "~0.25 Theta(x^1/4)"),
185	        ("prover wall",      [data[n]["wall"] for n in last], "see note"),
186	    ]
187	    print(f"{'metric':>20} {'alpha':>7}   expectation")
188	    for name, vals, exp in rows:
189	        a = _fit(last, vals)
190	        fits[name.strip()] = a
191	        print(f"{name:>20} {a:>7.3f}   {exp}")
192	    print("\nNOTE prover wall: measured alpha is overhead/call-count-bound "
193	          "(~sqrt x polylog;\n  S500/S501) at reachable n -- the asymptotic "
194	          "element-work is Õ(x) (S496/S497),\n  surfacing only past the "
195	          "array-size crossover.  Cert SIZE is the headline, not wall.")
196	
197	    # ---- headline + falsifiable assertions ----
198	    a_comm = fits["comm (cert size)"]
199	    a_outer = fits["comm_outer"]
200	    a_ver = fits["verifier ops"]
201	    out_frac = [data[n]["comm_outer"] / data[n]["comm"] for n in ns]
202	    assert 0.40 <= a_comm <= 0.65, ("comm exponent not ~sqrt x", a_comm)
203	    assert 0.40 <= a_outer <= 0.65, ("comm_outer exponent not ~sqrt x", a_outer)
204	    assert a_ver < 0.35, ("verifier-op exponent not ~x^1/4", a_ver)
205	    for nm in ("comm_bt", "comm_bw", "comm_ub", "comm_base"):

207	    assert out_frac[-1] > out_frac[0] and out_frac[-1] >= 0.80, \
208	        ("outer not the dominant / growing fraction", out_frac)
209	    print(f"\nHEADLINE: certificate SIZE alpha = {a_comm:.3f} ~ 0.5 "
210	          f"(Theta(sqrt x)); it is DOMINATED by the K SEQUENTIAL outer layer "
211	          f"reductions\n  (comm_outer alpha = {a_outer:.3f}, {100*out_frac[-1]:.0f}% "
212	          f"of comm at n={ns[-1]}, rising to 100%).  Every batchable obligation is "
213	          f"polylog;\n  the base commit is Theta(x^1/4); verifier large-table ops "
214	          f"alpha = {a_ver:.3f} ~ 0.25.\n  => L_pi has a CRH-based non-interactive "
215	          f"certificate of size Õ(sqrt x), verifiable with\n  Õ(x^1/4) large-table "
216	          f"opens (total verification Theta(sqrt x): the verifier reads the proof).\n"
217	          f"  The residual Õ(sqrt x) IS the floor(v/p)-semigroup sequential-layer "
218	          f"wall (open item 2).")
219	    return data

221	
222	def selftest():
223	    print("[selftest] certificate_profile (S509)")
224	    rng = np.random.default_rng
225	
226	    # 1. attribution sums EXACTLY to comm on COMPLETE (accepting) certificates --
227	    #    full, NOBW, and plain configs, over q AND BIG_Q.  Cheats (delta_pi,
228	    #    self-consistent liar) must still REJECT with the instrumentation present
229	    #    (a rejected transcript bails mid-layer, so partial comm is NOT a complete
230	    #    certificate and is not asserted to close -- by design).
231	    cfgs = {"full": FULL, "nobw": NOBW,
232	            "plain": dict(delegate=True, structured=True)}
233	    for n in (8, 10, 12):
234	        x = (1 << n) - 1; truth = cl.sieve_pi(x)
235	        K = len(cl.compressed_lucy(x)[0])
236	        for q in (cl.Q, cl.BIG_Q):
237	            for name, cfg in cfgs.items():
238	                r = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, **cfg)
239	                assert r["accepted"] and r["claimed"] == truth, (name, n, q)
240	                assert sum(r[k] for k in COMM_SRCS) == r["comm"], (name, n, q, "sum")
241	                # cheats: the run must REJECT (instrumentation is inert to verdict)
242	                rd = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, cheat="delta_pi", **cfg)
243	                assert not rd["accepted"], (name, n, q, "delta_pi accepted")
244	                i0 = max(1, K // 2)
245	                rl = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, corrupt_layer=i0, **cfg)
246	                assert not rl["accepted"], (name, n, q, "liar accepted")
247	    print("  1. attribution closes on complete certs (full/nobw/plain, q & BIG_Q);"
248	          " cheats reject OK")
249	
250	    # 2. comm COUNT (field elements) is field-independent (only bit-width differs);
251	    #    per-source counts match between q and BIG_Q too.
252	    for n in (8, 10, 12):
253	        x = (1 << n) - 1
254	        rq = cl.run_chain(x, rng(2), q=cl.Q, **FULL)
255	        rb = cl.run_chain(x, rng(2), q=cl.BIG_Q, **FULL)
256	        assert rq["comm"] == rb["comm"], (n, "comm count field-dependent")
257	        for k in COMM_SRCS:
258	            assert rq[k] == rb[k], (n, k, "per-source count field-dependent")
259	    print("  2. comm COUNT field-independent (q vs BIG_Q identical) OK")
260	
261	    # 3. with wiring batched, comm_outer is purely the outer reductions and is
262	    #    STRICTLY less than the NOBW config's comm_outer (which folds the inline
263	    #    wiring in) -- the batching demonstrably moves comm out of 'outer'.
264	    for n in (10, 12):
265	        x = (1 << n) - 1
266	        rf = cl.run_chain(x, rng(3), q=cl.Q, **FULL)
267	        rd = cl.run_chain(x, rng(3), q=cl.Q, **NOBW)
268	        assert rf["comm_outer"] < rd["comm_outer"], (n, rf["comm_outer"], rd["comm_outer"])
269	        assert rf["comm_bw"] > 0 and rd["comm_bw"] == 0, n     # bw only in full
270	        assert rf["comm"] < rd["comm"], (n, "batching wiring did not cut comm")
271	    print("  3. batch_wiring moves comm out of 'outer' and cuts total comm OK")
272	
273	    # 4. exponents on a short sweep (n=8..16): comm ~0.5, comm_outer ~0.5 and
274	    #    dominant+growing, batched discharges + verifier ops sub-0.4.
275	    ns = (8, 10, 12, 14, 16)
276	    data = measure(ns, FULL, cl.Q, seed=1)
277	    last = ns[-4:]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
certificate_profile.py -- S509.  Characterize the FULL non-interactive certificate
for "pi(x) = c" and LOCATE the Õ(sqrt x) communication wall.

CONTEXT.  By S508 the whole-chain VERIFIER's expensive sub-term -- the count of
large-table (mle_eval over a sqrt-x-size cube) evaluations -- is Õ(x^{1/4}) (the
two S_0 base closes go through the tensor PCS; every per-layer leaf open was
removed by pcs+batch_trace+batch_ub).  The verifier side of the milestone is met.
The quantity that is STILL Õ(sqrt x) is the certificate SIZE itself: stats["comm"]
(the Fiat-Shamir transcript) has slope ~0.5 in every config.  This file pins down
exactly WHERE that Õ(sqrt x) lives.

WHAT IS MEASURED (full succinct config = delegate+structured+pcs+batch_trace+
batch_ub+batch_wiring+commit_base, over n in {8..18}):
  (i)   certificate SIZE = total stats["comm"] in field elements AND in bits
        (bits = elems * ceil(log2 q); BIG_Q elems are 61-bit, Q elems 31-bit --
        a constant factor, same exponent);
  (ii)  verifier op-count = vleaf_ops_pl + vleaf_ops_ot (== vcommit_ops in this
        config -- the only LARGE-table work left is the one-time PCS base opens);
  (iii) prover wall.
Each exponent is fitted (alpha = d log2(metric) / d n, so alpha~1 => Theta(x),
alpha~0.5 => Theta(sqrt x), alpha~0.25 => Theta(x^{1/4})).

The full config STRICTLY EXTENDS the S508 "config (d)" named in PROGRAM.md by also
turning on batch_wiring (built S503/S504 precisely to cut comm ~5x): with the
wiring batched, comm_outer is PURELY the sequential two-sided layer reductions, the
cleanest form of the result.  We also print the no-batch_wiring variant to show the
conclusion is robust either way (there the batchable wiring is merely folded into
comm_outer, making it even more dominant).

ATTRIBUTION.  run_chain (S509) partitions stats["comm"] by source -- a purely
additive boundary-snapshot, transcript unchanged:
  comm_outer : the K = pi(sqrt x) SEQUENTIAL per-layer two-sided reductions
               (phase-A/phase-B outer sum-checks + the pcs line/claim folds).
  comm_bt    : the ONE batched trace zero-test (all K layers).
  comm_bw    : the ONE batched wiring discharge (all 2K-1 wirings).
  comm_ub    : the ONE batched Ub-opening discharge (all K*nb leaves).
  comm_base  : the two one-time S_0 closes (tensor-PCS eval proofs).
The five sum EXACTLY to stats["comm"] (asserted).

HEADLINE RESULT.  The Õ(sqrt x) certificate is DOMINATED by comm_outer (60% -> 90%
of the total as n: 8 -> 18, and -> 100% asymptotically): after EVERY batchable
obligation has been batched (trace/wiring/Ub -> polylog) and the base committed
(-> x^{1/4}), the only term left at Theta(sqrt x) is the K sequential layer
reductions.  comm_outer ~ K * nb^2 = pi(sqrt x) * O(log^2 x) = Theta(sqrt x polylog).

MEMBERSHIP STATEMENT this yields.  L_pi = {(x,c) : pi(x) = c} has, under a
collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle assumption (Fiat-Shamir of the chain), a
NON-INTERACTIVE certificate of size Õ(sqrt x) field elements (Õ(sqrt x * log^2 x)
bits), whose expensive (large-table) verifier work is Õ(x^{1/4}).  HONEST: the
verifier must READ the Õ(sqrt x) proof (each transcript scalar is an O(1) sum-check
round check), so TOTAL verification is Theta(sqrt x) -- bounded below by the proof
size.  The Õ(x^{1/4}) of S508 is the large-table-eval SUB-term only; this file makes
that explicit.  Compressing the SIZE (and hence total verification) below sqrt x to
polylog requires batching the K SEQUENTIAL outer reductions -- which hits the SAME
wall as open item 2 (the layer-batching closed negative): each layer's OUTPUT claim
is the next layer's INPUT claim, a dependency chain, unlike the trace/Ub/wiring
obligations (independent per-layer witnesses sharing one random trajectory, hence
batchable).  The semigroup generated by v |-> floor(v/p) is the precise obstruction.

FALSIFIERS (any one would break the result):
  * total comm exponent NOT ~0.5 (we assert it lands in [0.4, 0.65]);
  * the per-source attribution NOT summing to the measured comm (asserted exactly);
  * comm_outer NOT the dominant / growing fraction, or its exponent NOT ~0.5;
  * the batched-discharge / base exponents NOT sub-0.5 (they should be polylog or
    x^{1/4});
  * verifier-op exponent NOT ~0.25 (re-confirms S508);
  * claimed pi(x) differing from the sieve in any config / field;
  * a claimed batching of the SEQUENTIAL outer reductions that actually drops the
    comm exponent below 0.5 -- that would be a genuine breakthrough (it batches the
    floor(v/p) semigroup), NOT a measurement; verify it against open item 2 before
    believing it.

CLI:
  python3 certificate_profile.py --selftest
  python3 certificate_profile.py                 # the profile (default q, n=8..18)
  python3 certificate_profile.py --field big     # over BIG_Q=2^61-1 (61-bit elems)
"""
import argparse
import math
import time

import numpy as np

import compressed_layer as cl

# the minimal certificate: every batchable obligation batched, base committed.
FULL = dict(delegate=True, structured=True, pcs=True, batch_trace=True,
            batch_ub=True, batch_wiring=True, commit_base=True)
# the literal S508 "config (d)" -- wiring NOT batched (discharged inline per layer).
NOBW = dict(delegate=True, structured=True, pcs=True, batch_trace=True,
            batch_ub=True, commit_base=True)

COMM_SRCS = ["comm_outer", "comm_bt", "comm_bw", "comm_ub", "comm_base"]
FIELDS = {"q": cl.Q, "big": cl.BIG_Q}


def _verifier_ops(r):
    """Large-table (mle_eval / PCS) field-op count -- the S507/S508 metric."""
    return r["vleaf_ops_pl"] + r["vleaf_ops_ot"]


def measure(ns, cfg, q, seed=1, check_truth=True):
    """Run run_chain over ns with cfg; return {n: result} (result carries an
    added 'wall' and 'x').  Asserts accept, claimed==sieve, and that the comm
    attribution sums exactly to stats['comm']."""
    out = {}
    for n in ns:
        x = (1 << n) - 1
        t = time.perf_counter()
        r = cl.run_chain(x, np.random.default_rng(seed), q=q, **cfg)
        r["wall"] = time.perf_counter() - t
        r["x"] = x
        if check_truth:
            assert r["accepted"], (n, "rejected honest run")
            assert r["claimed"] == cl.sieve_pi(x), (n, r["claimed"])
        # attribution closes exactly
        parts = sum(r[k] for k in COMM_SRCS)
        assert parts == r["comm"], (n, "comm attribution gap", parts, r["comm"])
        out[n] = r
    return out


def _fit(ns, vals):
    return cl._fit_slope(list(ns), [math.log2(max(1, v)) for v in vals])


def profile(ns=(8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18), field="q", seed=1):
    q = FIELDS[field]
    bpe = q.bit_length()                       # bits per field element (31 / 61)
    print(f"=== certificate profile (full succinct config), field={field} "
          f"({bpe}-bit elems) ===")
    print("config = delegate+structured+pcs+batch_trace+batch_ub+batch_wiring"
          "+commit_base")
    data = measure(ns, FULL, q, seed)

    # ---- table 1: size / verifier ops / prover wall ----
    print("\n-- certificate SIZE, VERIFIER ops, PROVER wall --")
    print(f"{'n':>3} {'x':>9} {'V':>6} {'nb':>3} {'K':>4} {'pi':>7} | "
          f"{'cert_elems':>10} {'cert_KB':>8} | {'verif_ops':>9} | "
          f"{'prover_s':>8}")
    for n in ns:
        r = data[n]
        x = r["x"]; V = cl.isqrt(x); nb = max(1, V.bit_length()); K = r["layers"]
        kb = r["comm"] * bpe / 8 / 1024
        print(f"{n:>3} {x:>9} {V:>6} {nb:>3} {K:>4} {r['claimed']:>7} | "
              f"{r['comm']:>10} {kb:>8.2f} | {_verifier_ops(r):>9} | "
              f"{r['wall']:>8.3f}")

    # ---- table 2: per-source comm attribution ----
    print("\n-- comm ATTRIBUTION by source (field elements; outer = the K "
          "sequential layer reductions) --")
    print(f"{'n':>3} {'comm':>8} | {'outer':>8} {'out%':>5} | {'bt':>5} "
          f"{'bw':>6} {'ub':>5} {'base':>6}")
    for n in ns:
        r = data[n]
        pct = 100.0 * r["comm_outer"] / r["comm"]
        print(f"{n:>3} {r['comm']:>8} | {r['comm_outer']:>8} {pct:>4.0f}% | "
              f"{r['comm_bt']:>5} {r['comm_bw']:>6} {r['comm_ub']:>5} "
              f"{r['comm_base']:>6}")

    # ---- table 3: effect of batching the wiring (full vs S508 config (d)) ----
    print("\n-- comm: full (wiring batched) vs S508 config (d) (wiring inline) --")
    dnobw = measure(ns, NOBW, q, seed)
    print(f"{'n':>3} {'full_comm':>9} {'full_outer':>11} || "
          f"{'d_comm':>8} {'d_outer':>8}  (inline wiring folds into outer)")
    for n in ns:
        print(f"{n:>3} {data[n]['comm']:>9} {data[n]['comm_outer']:>11} || "
              f"{dnobw[n]['comm']:>8} {dnobw[n]['comm_outer']:>8}")

    # ---- exponent fits ----
    last = ns[-4:]
    print(f"\n-- fitted exponents alpha (metric ~ x^alpha; log2(metric) vs n, "
          f"last {len(last)} pts: n in {tuple(last)}) --")
    fits = {}
    rows = [
        ("comm (cert size)", [data[n]["comm"] for n in last], "~0.5  Theta(sqrt x)"),
        ("  comm_outer",     [data[n]["comm_outer"] for n in last], "~0.5  Theta(sqrt x)  <-- DOMINANT"),
        ("  comm_bt",        [data[n]["comm_bt"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
        ("  comm_bw",        [data[n]["comm_bw"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
        ("  comm_ub",        [data[n]["comm_ub"] for n in last], "polylog (sub-0.5)"),
        ("  comm_base",      [data[n]["comm_base"] for n in last], "~0.25 Theta(x^1/4) PCS"),
        ("verifier ops",     [_verifier_ops(data[n]) for n in last], "~0.25 Theta(x^1/4)"),
        ("prover wall",      [data[n]["wall"] for n in last], "see note"),
    ]
    print(f"{'metric':>20} {'alpha':>7}   expectation")
    for name, vals, exp in rows:
        a = _fit(last, vals)
        fits[name.strip()] = a
        print(f"{name:>20} {a:>7.3f}   {exp}")
    print("\nNOTE prover wall: measured alpha is overhead/call-count-bound "
          "(~sqrt x polylog;\n  S500/S501) at reachable n -- the asymptotic "
          "element-work is Õ(x) (S496/S497),\n  surfacing only past the "
          "array-size crossover.  Cert SIZE is the headline, not wall.")

    # ---- headline + falsifiable assertions ----
    a_comm = fits["comm (cert size)"]
    a_outer = fits["comm_outer"]
    a_ver = fits["verifier ops"]
    out_frac = [data[n]["comm_outer"] / data[n]["comm"] for n in ns]
    assert 0.40 <= a_comm <= 0.65, ("comm exponent not ~sqrt x", a_comm)
    assert 0.40 <= a_outer <= 0.65, ("comm_outer exponent not ~sqrt x", a_outer)
    assert a_ver < 0.35, ("verifier-op exponent not ~x^1/4", a_ver)
    for nm in ("comm_bt", "comm_bw", "comm_ub", "comm_base"):
        assert fits[nm] < a_outer, (nm, "not sub-dominant to outer", fits[nm], a_outer)
    assert out_frac[-1] > out_frac[0] and out_frac[-1] >= 0.80, \
        ("outer not the dominant / growing fraction", out_frac)
    print(f"\nHEADLINE: certificate SIZE alpha = {a_comm:.3f} ~ 0.5 "
          f"(Theta(sqrt x)); it is DOMINATED by the K SEQUENTIAL outer layer "
          f"reductions\n  (comm_outer alpha = {a_outer:.3f}, {100*out_frac[-1]:.0f}% "
          f"of comm at n={ns[-1]}, rising to 100%).  Every batchable obligation is "
          f"polylog;\n  the base commit is Theta(x^1/4); verifier large-table ops "
          f"alpha = {a_ver:.3f} ~ 0.25.\n  => L_pi has a CRH-based non-interactive "
          f"certificate of size Õ(sqrt x), verifiable with\n  Õ(x^1/4) large-table "
          f"opens (total verification Theta(sqrt x): the verifier reads the proof).\n"
          f"  The residual Õ(sqrt x) IS the floor(v/p)-semigroup sequential-layer "
          f"wall (open item 2).")
    return data


def selftest():
    print("[selftest] certificate_profile (S509)")
    rng = np.random.default_rng

    # 1. attribution sums EXACTLY to comm on COMPLETE (accepting) certificates --
    #    full, NOBW, and plain configs, over q AND BIG_Q.  Cheats (delta_pi,
    #    self-consistent liar) must still REJECT with the instrumentation present
    #    (a rejected transcript bails mid-layer, so partial comm is NOT a complete
    #    certificate and is not asserted to close -- by design).
    cfgs = {"full": FULL, "nobw": NOBW,
            "plain": dict(delegate=True, structured=True)}
    for n in (8, 10, 12):
        x = (1 << n) - 1; truth = cl.sieve_pi(x)
        K = len(cl.compressed_lucy(x)[0])
        for q in (cl.Q, cl.BIG_Q):
            for name, cfg in cfgs.items():
                r = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, **cfg)
                assert r["accepted"] and r["claimed"] == truth, (name, n, q)
                assert sum(r[k] for k in COMM_SRCS) == r["comm"], (name, n, q, "sum")
                # cheats: the run must REJECT (instrumentation is inert to verdict)
                rd = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, cheat="delta_pi", **cfg)
                assert not rd["accepted"], (name, n, q, "delta_pi accepted")
                i0 = max(1, K // 2)
                rl = cl.run_chain(x, rng(1), q=q, corrupt_layer=i0, **cfg)
                assert not rl["accepted"], (name, n, q, "liar accepted")
    print("  1. attribution closes on complete certs (full/nobw/plain, q & BIG_Q);"
          " cheats reject OK")

    # 2. comm COUNT (field elements) is field-independent (only bit-width differs);
    #    per-source counts match between q and BIG_Q too.
    for n in (8, 10, 12):
        x = (1 << n) - 1
        rq = cl.run_chain(x, rng(2), q=cl.Q, **FULL)
        rb = cl.run_chain(x, rng(2), q=cl.BIG_Q, **FULL)
        assert rq["comm"] == rb["comm"], (n, "comm count field-dependent")
        for k in COMM_SRCS:
            assert rq[k] == rb[k], (n, k, "per-source count field-dependent")
    print("  2. comm COUNT field-independent (q vs BIG_Q identical) OK")

    # 3. with wiring batched, comm_outer is purely the outer reductions and is
    #    STRICTLY less than the NOBW config's comm_outer (which folds the inline
    #    wiring in) -- the batching demonstrably moves comm out of 'outer'.
    for n in (10, 12):
        x = (1 << n) - 1
        rf = cl.run_chain(x, rng(3), q=cl.Q, **FULL)
        rd = cl.run_chain(x, rng(3), q=cl.Q, **NOBW)
        assert rf["comm_outer"] < rd["comm_outer"], (n, rf["comm_outer"], rd["comm_outer"])
        assert rf["comm_bw"] > 0 and rd["comm_bw"] == 0, n     # bw only in full
        assert rf["comm"] < rd["comm"], (n, "batching wiring did not cut comm")
    print("  3. batch_wiring moves comm out of 'outer' and cuts total comm OK")

    # 4. exponents on a short sweep (n=8..16): comm ~0.5, comm_outer ~0.5 and
    #    dominant+growing, batched discharges + verifier ops sub-0.4.
    ns = (8, 10, 12, 14, 16)
    data = measure(ns, FULL, cl.Q, seed=1)
    last = ns[-4:]
    a_comm = _fit(last, [data[n]["comm"] for n in last])
    a_outer = _fit(last, [data[n]["comm_outer"] for n in last])
    a_bw = _fit(last, [data[n]["comm_bw"] for n in last])
    a_ver = _fit(last, [_verifier_ops(data[n]) for n in last])
    frac = [data[n]["comm_outer"] / data[n]["comm"] for n in ns]
    assert 0.40 <= a_comm <= 0.65, a_comm
    assert 0.40 <= a_outer <= 0.65, a_outer
    assert a_bw < 0.40 and a_bw < a_outer, (a_bw, a_outer)
    # verifier large-table ops grow STRICTLY slower than the cert size (sub-sqrt-x);
    # the tight ~0.25 (Theta(x^1/4)) only settles past nb~14 (n~28, S508) -- on this
    # short sweep the t-query / reshape constant still inflates it, so bound loosely.
    assert a_ver < a_comm and a_ver < 0.45, (a_ver, a_comm)
    assert frac[-1] > frac[0] and frac[-1] >= 0.80, frac
    print(f"  4. exponents OK (comm {a_comm:.2f}, outer {a_outer:.2f} dom "
          f"{100*frac[-1]:.0f}%, bw {a_bw:.2f}, verif {a_ver:.2f})")

    # 5. verifier large-table ops in the full config are ENTIRELY one-time (the
    #    PCS base opens): per-layer leaf count 0, ops == vcommit_ops.
    for n in (8, 12, 16):
        x = (1 << n) - 1
        r = cl.run_chain(x, rng(4), q=cl.Q, **FULL)
        assert r["vleaf_cnt_pl"] == 0, (n, r["vleaf_cnt_pl"])
        assert r["vleaf_ops_pl"] == 0, (n, r["vleaf_ops_pl"])
        assert r["vcommit_ops"] == r["vleaf_ops_ot"] > 0, (n,)
    print("  5. verifier large-table work is one-time only (vleaf_pl=0) OK")

    print("[selftest] PASS")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--field", choices=list(FIELDS), default="q",
                    help="prime field: q=2^31-1 (31-bit), big=2^61-1 (61-bit)")
    ap.add_argument("--nmax", type=int, default=18, help="largest n (even)")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.selftest:
        selftest()
    else:
        ns = tuple(range(8, args.nmax + 1, 2))
        profile(ns, field=args.field, seed=args.seed)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

5	literature) on the VERIFICATION complexity of the prime-counting
6	function, as opposed to its computation complexity. Implemented,

9

11	
12	| protocol | verifies | verifier | prover | status |
13	|---|---|---|---|---|
14	| wheel sum-check | Φ(x, polylog wheel) | polylog | Θ̃(x) | built; 100/100 cheaters rejected |
15	| Lucy base | exact π(x) | Õ(x/log x) | Õ(x^{3/2}) | built; π(2²⁰−1) = 82025 verified; 50/50 rejected |
16	| Lucy + delegated wiring | exact π(x) | **Õ(√x)** | Õ(x^{3/2}) | built; crossover p ≈ 130 measured |

20	sieve layers, verifier < 1 s, transcript ~110 KB, soundness
21	information-theoretic (no crypto, no setup), with self-consistent
22	cheating provers — including DP-table corruption recomputed coherently
23	downstream, and false wiring claims — rejected in every trial.
24	
25	## Summary
26	
27	Every barrier catalogued by this project — the √x hard zone, the
28	GUE-random incompressible digits, the 730+ closed computation routes —
29	constrains *computing* π(x) from scratch. None of it constrains
30	*checking* a claimed value produced by a prover who did the work. That
31	asymmetry is real and exploitable:
32	
33	> **Protocol (S491).** An untrusted prover who runs the Lucy_Hedgehog
34	> sieve DP can convince a verifier of the EXACT value of π(x) with
35	> unconditional (information-theoretic) soundness — no hardness
36	> assumptions, no trusted setup. The verifier checks each of the
37	> K = π(√x) sieve layers by a degree-≤3 sum-check and never touches
38	> any Θ(x)-size object. Verifier cost: Õ(n·Σ_{p≤√x} p) field ops with
39	> automaton wiring (designed improvement to Õ(√x) via carry-chain
40	> wiring); communication Õ(K·n); soundness error ≤ ~7nK/q.
41	
42	Measured (q = 2³¹−1): π(65535) = 6542, π(262143) = 23000,
43	π(1048575) = 82025 all verified exactly; verifier 69 ms → 0.9 s while
44	x grows 16×; transcripts 28–110 KB; **50/50 cheating provers rejected**,
45	including self-consistent liars that corrupt one DP entry and recompute
46	all downstream layers coherently.
47	
48	## The two structural observations that make it work
49	
50	1. **The sieve recursion is made of small-automaton predicates.** The
51	   verifier's bottleneck in any sum-check is evaluating the multilinear
52	   extension (MLE) of the summand at a random field point. The MLE of
53	   the *primality indicator* is dense — 0.71 nonzero-coefficient
54	   fraction, 2^{n/2} coefficients (S48 / E2.1) — which is precisely why
55	   sum-check-for-computing-π(x) died at S18/S48. But the Lucy recurrence
56	   `S_i(v) = S_{i−1}(v) − [v ≥ p_i²]·(S_{i−1}(⌊v/p_i⌋) − (i−1))`
57	   contains no primality predicate: floor-division ⌊v/p⌋ is a p-state
58	   long-division automaton, the threshold [v ≥ p²] a 3-state comparator,
59	   and any width-W bit-automaton predicate has an MLE evaluable at an
60	   arbitrary point in O(n·W) by a transfer-matrix DP. **The sieve is
61	   verification-friendly because it decomposes primality into automaton
62	   steps; primality as a monolithic predicate is not.** This is a new
63	   counterpoint to E2.1: the same density wall that blocks computing
64	   blocks nothing once the predicate is factored through the recursion.
65	2. **The Lucy correction scalar is public.** S_{i−1}(p_i − 1) = i − 1
66	   (the primes below p_i), so each layer needs no extra prover claim
67	   for its correction term — the layer reductions chain with only two
68	   point-claims (merged by line restriction) and terminate in the
69	   closed form S̃_0(z) = Int(z) − 1 + Π(1−z_j).
70	
71	## Corollaries
72	
73	- **Succinct certificates for p(n).** "p(n) = y" is certified by (i) an
74	  ECPP/Pratt primality certificate for y, plus (ii) this protocol run
75	  on π(y) = n. Kilobyte-scale, unconditionally sound up to the field
76	  soundness error. Today's trust mechanism for record π(x) values is
77	  independent recomputation by a different algorithm; this replaces
78	  months of recomputation with a transcript.
79	- **Certified comparisons in the hard zone.** The decision problem
80	  [p(n) ≤ x?] ⟺ [π(x) ≥ n?] is worst-case as hard as computing p(n)
81	  (binary search, E6.6), and inside the √x-wide hard window around
82	  R⁻¹(n) each comparison costs a full π(x) computation. But it is
83	  cheaply *verifiable*: a prover can certify each comparison bit.
84	  Empirical geography of the decision problem measured in
85	  `experiments/analytic/guess_comparison_oracle/`: against the biased
86	  guess li⁻¹(n) the comparison bit is constant (30/30, the
87	  Rubinstein–Sarnak bias, predictable up to the Skewes scale ~10³¹⁶);
88	  against the centered guess R⁻¹(n) it is an empirical coin flip
89	  (10/30 vs 20/30) — the better the guess, the closer the bit is to
90	  fair, which is the information barrier restated.
91	- **The verification-complexity landscape (corrected S491-late).** In
92	  principle, GKR 2008 over the data-parallel uniform primality circuit
93	  (Σ over w ≤ x of an AKS copy — polylog depth, log-space uniform)
94	  already gives an unconditionally-sound interactive proof with polylog
95	  verifier and poly(x) prover — a literature corollary, NOT novel, and
96	  with astronomically large polylog constants and a nontrivial
97	  wiring-uniformity verification. (An earlier draft of this file
98	  posed "polylog or √x floor?" as open; the in-principle answer is
99	  polylog, by GKR.) The honest open questions are: (a) a *practical*
100	  polylog-verifier protocol — the S491 Lucy protocol runs in
101	  milliseconds but its wiring totals Õ(x/log x); **the delegated-wiring
102	  upgrade (built and measured S491-late,
103	  `lucy_dp_delegated_wiring.py`) reaches Õ(√x)**: the division
104	  automaton's DP is itself GKR-delegated, the verifier evaluating the
105	  transition relation s′ = 2s + a − b·p via a width-4 carry automaton
106	  in O(log p) — measured 3.2× verifier growth over an 84× p-range (vs
107	  34× for the automaton baseline, whose linear-in-p cost the
108	  width-dichotomy theorem proves unavoidable without delegation);
109	  crossover at p ≈ 130. The remaining √x → polylog gap is now exactly
110	  the K = π(√x) sequential layer structure of the sieve itself;
111	  (b) succinct *non-interactive* certificates unconditionally — made
112	  precise (S491-late): a polylog-size unconditionally-checkable
113	  certificate for π(x) = c is exactly the statement
114	  **L_π = {(x, c) : π(x) = c} ∈ NP** in input length n = log x.
115	  No construction is known (even the "≥ c" direction lacks a succinct
116	  witness — listing primes costs ~x bits; Pratt/ECPP certify one
117	  prime, not a count), and no barrier either: for #P-complete
118	  functions, value-certificates in NP would force NP = coNP, but π(x)
119	  is not known #P-hard (proving THAT would itself be a major result,
120	  and is a cleaner formal target than the algorithmic question).
121	  L_π ∈ NP is the proof-theoretic shadow of the headline problem:
122	  polylog computation would trivially imply polylog certificates, so
123	  certificate lower bounds are the easier-to-attack face of the same
124	  wall; (c) the constructibility dichotomy below.
125	
126	## The width spectrum (S491 brainstorm follow-up, measured)
127	
128	`experiments/constructions/automaton_width_dichotomy/` upgrades the
129	project's OBDD-width edge from a computation lower bound to an exact
130	verification-cost measure: given an explicit read-once branching
131	program with cut-widths (W_j), the MLE is evaluable at any field point
132	in O(Σ_j W_j) (transfer DP — Theorem T1, implemented). Measured at
133	x = 2²⁴ with matched-random control:
134	
135	- **Division wiring [u = ⌊v/p⌋] has Nerode width exactly 2p+1** —
136	  the S491 protocol's O(n·p) wiring check is optimal among explicit
137	  automatons; prover-supplied carry witnesses are *necessary* (not just
138	  sufficient) to go below.
139	- **χ_P's width profile = incompressible plateau + admissibility
140	  cliff**: W_j = 2^j exactly through j = 16 (every aligned 256-window
141	  of primes distinct — the global pseudorandom side), then a crash to
142	  44× below random (107 vs 4707 distinct aligned 16-windows — wheel/HL
143	  local rigidity made quantitative). The cut-profile invariant
144	  D_k(x) = #distinct aligned k-windows of χ_P is new to the project
145	  and bridges its global-randomness and local-structure edge families
146	  in one curve.
147	- **Middle-cut width is maximal (2^{n/2} = 4096 > E2.1 rank 2050)** —
148	  refines the rank edge: the factor-2 deficiency is linear-algebraic,
149	  not informational.
150	- **One-shot sum-check verification of π(x) is dead twice over**:
151	  Σ_j W_j(χ_P) ~ x^c with c drifting 0.73 → 0.77 upward (peak-crossover
152	  argument gives c → 1), AND the minimal program is non-constructible
153	  without the primes. Verification must consume primality through
154	  explicit small-width sieve predicates — layering is structurally
155	  forced, which is exactly what the Lucy protocol does.
156	- **The cliff is exactly Hardy-Littlewood (S491 continuation,
157	  `experiments/analytic/local_pattern_census/`).** W_j = D_k(2ⁿ)
158	  (k = 2^{n−j}) by definition, and the census saturates at
159	  **D_k(x) = A_k + 1** — the exactly-enumerable count of HL-admissible
160	  aligned patterns, plus the single m = 0 window containing the small
161	  primes. Verified to closure: k = 8 (14 = 13+1), k = 16 (107 = 106+1,
162	  all admissible realized by x = 2¹⁸, stable through 2²⁸); k = 32
163	  converging (3385 of A₃₂+1 = 3574 at 2²⁶; the 189 missing are exactly
164	  the weight ≥ 6 dense constellations — the census deficit is a
165	  finite-x probe of k-tuple uniformity). Max weights 3/5/9 match the
166	  classical H(k) narrowest-tuple function. **The prime indicator's
167	  width spectrum = global-pseudorandom plateau + admissible-pattern
168	  entropy curve**, with the crossover set by the (open) entropy
169	  constant lim log₂(A_k)/k (measured 0.46 → 0.37 at k = 8 → 32).
170	
171	## Honest scope
172	
173	- No speedup for computing π(x); the prover pays the full sieve cost.
174	  This is an adjacent-problem partial-positive in the S224 mold —
175	  computation unchanged, trust exponentially cheaper.
176	- The protocol composes standard tools (LFKN 1992 sum-check; GKR-style
177	  layer reductions; CMT 2012 prover techniques). The novelty is the
178	  application target (no prior verification protocol for π(x) exists),
179	  the automaton-MLE treatment of the sieve wiring, and the public-
180	  scalar observation that makes the Lucy chain close without auxiliary
181	  claims.
182	- Demo field q = 2³¹−1 (soundness ~10⁻⁶ at n=16). **Field lift (S498,
183	  corrected):** the multiply-trace identity U·a+R−X=0 is sound only while
184	  the field's CHARACTERISTIC exceeds the integers it relates (U·a ~ x),
185	  i.e. q > x, roughly n ≲ 30. The lift is therefore to a larger-
186	  characteristic PRIME (q ~ 2⁶¹−1 for n ≲ 60, generic ~128-bit prime for
187	  cryptographic x) — NOT an extension field. An extension field F_{q²} has
188	  q² *elements* but characteristic q, so an aliasing forgery (off by k·q)
189	  embeds as the SAME field element as the truth and is undetectable; the
190	  larger element count only shrinks Schwartz–Zippel error, an orthogonal
191	  concern. Demonstrated end-to-end in `compressed_prover_mult_trace.py`
192	  (`--field`, `--alias-demo`, `--refute-q2`). The genuine alternative to a
193	  bigger prime is a small-field schoolbook carry trace. **The lift is now
194	  threaded through the WHOLE compressed chain (S499):** `compressed_layer.py`
195	  `run_chain` and the delegated wiring (`lucy_dp_delegated_wiring.py`) carry a
196	  prime-modulus `q` (`--field {q,big,small}`), default `q=2³¹−1` bit-identical,
197	  `q=2⁶¹−1` over exact-int object arrays — the chain over `big` gives
198	  `claimed π==sieve` with all cheats rejected, and the wrap-around alias the demo
199	  prime admits is rejected by the lift in the chain's exact trace config. The
200	  remaining gap to a large-n run is speed, not soundness — but (**S500**) the
201	  obvious speed fix is not the bottleneck: the numpy `2⁶¹−1` mulmod
202	  (`_mul61`/`_sum61`, `2⁶¹≡1` fold) is built and threaded chain-wide
203	  bit-identically, yet it is a *large-array-only* win (the single-`√x`-cube
204	  certifier gains 1.7–3.8× at n=24–28; the **full chain is slower**, being
205	  `π(√x)` layers of many small cubes — *operation-count-bound*, not
206	  width-bound). The pure-Python Lucy DP is also negligible (`<0.1%` of
207	  `run_chain`). So the real lever for a fast large-x chain run is reducing the
208	  *count* of small per-layer field-ops (cross-cube batching), kept opt-in
209	  (`--fast-big`) with BIG_Q on the object reference by default.
210	  Demo prover is table-based Θ(2ⁿ/layer); production prover works the O(√x)
211	  compressed Lucy state at Õ(x) total.
212	- **Leaf openings (S505).** Each layer's claim is grounded by opening a committed
213	  O(√x)-size MLE at a point. The demo closed these by direct `mle_eval`
214	  (O(√x) each → O(K·√x) ≈ Õ(x) over the chain, the last √x-/p-linear verifier
215	  term). `leaf_open.py` builds the standard **sum-check opening** — `S~(pt)=Σ_w
216	  S[w]eq~(pt,w)` is itself a degree-2 sum-check — reducing an opening at `pt` to a
217	  polylog transcript (verifier O(nb)) plus ONE residual claim at a fresh point.
218	  `run_chain(--pcs)` threads each fold's residual as the next layer's carried
219	  claim, discharged transitively at the S₀ base — **unconditional** (no
220	  commitment; soundness rides the GKR layer reductions). Measured: the standalone
221	  opening verifier is flat in 2^nb (6.5×→432× over `mle_eval` as nb grows;
222	  21×→3605× over BIG_Q); the chain integration is a **stable ~1.2–1.36× verifier
223	  win**, NOT yet asymptotic — the remaining per-layer O(2^nb) term is the trace
224	  region's nb Ub-bit-table openings (per-layer witness data, no carried claim to
225	  thread to), which want the batched-trace integration. A real multilinear
226	  commitment (Brakedown/FRI-free) would discharge all residuals succinctly under a
227	  hashing assumption, trading unconditionality for full succinctness.
228	- **Batched Ub openings (S506) — the per-layer verifier is now leaf-eval-free.**
229	  That one remaining per-layer O(2^nb) term is closed. The nb Ub-bit-table openings
230	  `Ub_{Lv−nb+k}~(r_C)` (the B2 routing that pins g1_trace to the certified quotient
231	  u_e) are EXACTLY the tables the batched trace zero-test (`batched_trace`,
232	  `verify_constraints_batched`) already stacks and commits along the layer axis, so
233	  the discharge SHARES that commitment. Each layer defers `(l, r_C^l, [ub_{l,k}])`
234	  (the prover supplies the scalars; the verifier folds them into B2's `expect` in
235	  O(nb)) and all K·nb discharge in **ONE degree-2 sum-check**: with γ←F_q, β=γ^nb the
236	  weight β^l·γ^k=γ^{l·nb+k} is a distinct power, and the identity factorizes to a
237	  single inner product `Σ_w B[w]·C[w]` over the (Lk+nb)-cube — B the verifier-anchored
238	  per-layer eq weights (the soundness anchor, recomputed in O(K(Lk+nb))), C the γ-fold
239	  of the committed low-nb Ub tables (its opening taken from the sum-check's folded
240	  scalar, exactly as the zero-test trusts its bit scalars). `verify_ub_openings_batched`;
241	  wired behind `run_chain(--pcs --batch_trace --batch_ub)`. **Measured: the verifier-
242	  side O(2^nb) Ub-leaf eval count drops K·nb→0 at every n** (moved to the prover); the
243	  per-layer verifier is leaf-eval-free, so the only O(√x) verifier work left is
244	  one-time — the two S₀ base closes plus the batched discharges. **The unconditional
245	  Õ(√x) end-to-end verifier is now structurally real.** Honest scope: the wall-clock
246	  t_verifier win is a modest ~1.1–1.2× and flat in n (a vectorised numpy `mle_eval`
247	  over a √x-size array is cheap relative to the Python-loop wiring/eq recomputes that
248	  dominate the measured t_verifier), so the asymptotic O(K·nb·2^nb)→one-time gain is in
249	  **op-count, not measured wall-clock** at reachable n — correcting the S505 prediction
250	  that the verifier ratio would grow with n. Only a real outer commitment for the two
251	  one-time S₀ base closes remains (computational, not unconditional).
252	- **Tensor polynomial commitment for the base closes (S508) — the whole-chain
253	  verifier is now sub-√x.** That last one-time term is closed. `pcs_commit.py` is a
254	  hash-based multilinear PCS (Ligero/Brakedown tensor style): reshape the 2^nb table
255	  into an r×k matrix (r=2^{n1}, k=2^{n2}, n1+n2=nb), RS-encode each row, Merkle-commit
256	  the N columns (sha256 = CRH/RO stand-in). Using `eq~(pt,w)=eq~(pt_hi,w_hi)·eq~(pt_lo,
257	  w_lo)` so `S~(pt)=a^T M b` (a=eq_table(pt_hi), b=eq_table(pt_lo)), the **evaluation-
258	  proof verifier is O(t·(r+k)) = O(x^{1/4}·polylog)** — sub-√x: it reads the two
259	  combined messages v=a^T M, w=ρ^T M (len k), checks the eval binding ⟨v,b⟩=claimed,
260	  and at t Fiat–Shamir columns checks Merkle membership + the linear-code consistency
261	  Enc(v)[c]=⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩, Enc(w)[c]=⟨ρ,Mhat[:,c]⟩. The full 2^nb table never touches
262	  the verifier. Wired behind `run_chain(--commit-base)`; with `--pcs --batch_trace
263	  --batch_ub --commit-base` the **whole-chain verifier is sub-√x**. Measured
264	  (`--bench-verifier-ops`, config d): leading-term exponent **α_ops = 0.258 ≈ 0.25
265	  (Θ(x^{1/4}))**, vs config c's 0.500 (Θ(√x)) — the milestone drop Θ(x)→Θ(√x)→Θ(x^{1/4}).
266	  Verdict unchanged over q AND BIG_Q (honest π==sieve, delta_pi + self-consistent liar
267	  rejected); cheating-prover tests reject wrong claim / forged opening / tampered
268	  codeword row / tampered revealed column. **Honest scope:** this trades the otherwise-
269	  unconditional Õ(√x) verifier for full succinctness under the hash assumption (the rest
270	  of the verifier stays unconditional); the win is the SLOPE — the absolute op count
271	  only drops below the direct 2^nb close at nb≈14 (n≈28), the t-query constant dominating
272	  below that (the S506 crossover pattern); and RS's N≤q point requirement is a demo
273	  artifact that a field-size-free linear code (Brakedown's expander code) removes behind
274	  the same interface.
275	- **Certificate SIZE characterized — the Õ(√x) comm wall localized (S509).** With the
276	  verifier's large-table work down to Õ(x^{1/4}), the binding Õ(√x) quantity is the
277	  certificate SIZE itself (the Fiat–Shamir transcript, `stats["comm"]`, slope ~0.5 in
278	  every config). `certificate_profile.py` measures the full succinct config
279	  (delegate+structured+pcs+batch_trace+batch_ub+**batch_wiring**+commit_base) over
280	  n∈{8..18}: cert size **α=0.473 (Θ(√x))**, verifier ops **α=0.258 (Θ(x^{1/4}))**, prover
281	  wall α=0.41 (overhead-bound at reachable n; asymptotic element-work Õ(x)). `run_chain`
282	  now partitions `comm` by source (additive snapshots, sum==comm asserted); the Õ(√x) is
283	  **DOMINATED by `comm_outer` (α=0.522, 60%→90%→100% of comm) = the K=π(√x) SEQUENTIAL
284	  outer two-sided layer reductions** (each O(nb²)=O(log²x) round scalars × K=π(√x) ⇒
285	  Θ(√x·polylog)); every batched discharge (trace/wiring/Ub) is polylog (α≤0.18), the base
286	  commit Θ(x^{1/4}). Batching the wiring (S503/S504) cuts comm 5.3× at n=18 — the reason it
287	  is in the headline config. **Honest sharpening of S508:** the verifier must READ the
288	  Õ(√x) proof (each transcript scalar is an O(1) round check), so **total verification is
289	  Θ(√x)** — bounded below by the proof size; the S508 Õ(x^{1/4}) is the large-table-eval
290	  SUB-term only. **Membership result:** `L_π = {(x,c) : π(x)=c}` has, under a CRH/RO
291	  (Fiat–Shamir of the chain), a NON-INTERACTIVE certificate of size **Õ(√x)** field
292	  elements (Õ(√x·log²x) bits) with **Õ(x^{1/4})** large-table opens. Compressing the size
293	  (hence total verification) below √x to polylog requires batching the K SEQUENTIAL outer
294	  reductions — but each layer's OUTPUT claim is the next layer's INPUT claim (a dependency
295	  chain), unlike the independent per-layer trace/Ub/wiring witnesses that WERE batchable.
296	  That is exactly the ⌊v/p⌋-semigroup compression — the layer-batching closed negative
297	  (open problem 2). **The certificate-size wall and the prover-time wall are the same
298	  sequential-sieve wall, on the two faces of the problem.**
299	
300	## Open problems (the verification program, consolidated S491-final)
301	
302	1. **Compressed prover** — make the prover pay Õ(x) (polylog overhead
303	   over plain Lucy) instead of Õ(x^{3/2}). The large-value side forces
304	   d-addressing whose cross-map u = ⌊x/(dp)⌋ is variable×variable
305	   multiplication ⟹ a trace-table (AIR-style) GKR. **Step 1 built and
306	   tested (S492):** `compressed_prover_mult_trace.py` — a batched
307	   primitive verifying C = Σ_d eq(ρ,d)·S̃(⌊X/(dp)⌋) with every quotient
308	   certified through prover trace tables (a degree-3 constraint
309	   zero-test — multiply+remainder identity, bit-range recompositions,
310	   remainder bound — plus a routing lookup), verifier polylog O(m·Lv)
311	   and never dividing, prover on the D≈√x cube; 6 cheat classes
312	   rejected, verifier flat in batch size. Remaining: integrate into the
313	   layer protocol (small/large-side dispatch; the affine index map for
314	   dp≤√x; chaining and line-batching the S̃ claims).
315	2. **Layer batching (closed negative, S491-final).** Merging the
316	   K = π(√x) sequential layers by a balanced product tree fails on
317	   fill-in: each layer matrix has fill ≤ 3 per row on the compressed
318	   state space, but a j-layer merge has fill ~2^j per row (one entry
319	   per subset-product ⌊v/(p_{i₁}···p_{iₛ})⌋; K < |V| so fill never
320	   saturates). Sparse-multiplication cost at tree level ℓ is
321	   K·m·2^{ℓ−1} — geometric, top-dominated: **m·K²/2 ≈ x^{3/2}/ln²x**,
322	   no better than the unbatched prover. Polylog-depth verification
323	   with Õ(x) prover therefore requires algebraic compression of the
324	   semigroup generated by the maps v ↦ ⌊v/p⌋ — open, and the precise
325	   form of the project's √x sequential-sieve wall on the verification
326	   side.
327	3. **L_π ∈ NP?** (see above) — succinct unconditional non-interactive
328	   certificates; no construction, no barrier. The complementary formal
329	   target: **is π(x) #P-hard?** Either answer would be major; hardness
330	   would explain the project's whole closure landscape. **Concrete upper
331	   bound (S509):** L_π has a *computational* (CRH/RO) non-interactive
332	   certificate of size **Õ(√x)** — far short of polylog, and the Õ(√x) is
333	   provably (measured) the K=π(√x) sequential layer reductions, i.e. the
334	   open-problem-2 semigroup wall. So the unconditional-polylog question and
335	   the layer-batching question are the same wall; a sub-√x certificate (even
336	   computational) would already be new.
337	4. **A_k entropy law at k = 128** — the census conjecture
338	   A_k = e^{(1+o(1))π(k)} is enumeration-verified to k = 64 (clean
339	   2-power family, geometric convergence to constant ≈ 1); k = 128 has
340	   A ~ e²⁵ and needs an analytic count (the surjection inclusion-
341	   exclusion suffers catastrophic cancellation; the DFS is
342	   enumeration-bound). A transfer-matrix or generating-function attack
343	   is the well-posed successor.
344	5. **Large-x benchmark** — once (1) lands: verify π(10⁹⁺) and measure
345	   the verifier-vs-recomputation crossover against primecount-class
346	   baselines; the asymptotic separation is already measured at the
347	   wiring level (3.2× vs 34× over an 84× p-range).
348	
349	## Cross-references
350	
351	E2.1 (MLE density — circumvented, not contradicted), E6.6 (binary
352	search), S18 + S48 CLOSED_PATHS rows (scope-corrected: they close
353	computation, not verification), S224 (partial-positive prototype),
354	OPEN_POSITIVE_TARGETS.md §P12 / ATTACK_VECTORS.md §H5 (Thread 12),
355	`experiments/constructions/p12_sumcheck_pi_verification/` (code, logs,
356	falsifiers), `experiments/analytic/guess_comparison_oracle/` (decision-
357	problem geography).

# Novel Finding: Exact π(x) Is Succinctly Verifiable — the Computation/Verification Dichotomy

**Status:** Novel construction + working protocols (S491). First attack
in the project (and, per S491 + S48 literature searches, first in the
literature) on the VERIFICATION complexity of the prime-counting
function, as opposed to its computation complexity. Implemented,
tested, adversarially exercised:
`experiments/constructions/p12_sumcheck_pi_verification/`.

## The protocol stack (all unconditionally sound; all measured)

| protocol | verifies | verifier | prover | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wheel sum-check | Φ(x, polylog wheel) | polylog | Θ̃(x) | built; 100/100 cheaters rejected |
| Lucy base | exact π(x) | Õ(x/log x) | Õ(x^{3/2}) | built; π(2²⁰−1) = 82025 verified; 50/50 rejected |
| Lucy + delegated wiring | exact π(x) | **Õ(√x)** | Õ(x^{3/2}) | built; crossover p ≈ 130 measured |
| GKR-over-AKS | exact π(x) | polylog | poly(x) | literature corollary (GKR'08 + AKS); impractical constants |

Headline measured row: exact π(1048575) = 82025 verified through 172
sieve layers, verifier < 1 s, transcript ~110 KB, soundness
information-theoretic (no crypto, no setup), with self-consistent
cheating provers — including DP-table corruption recomputed coherently
downstream, and false wiring claims — rejected in every trial.

## Summary

Every barrier catalogued by this project — the √x hard zone, the
GUE-random incompressible digits, the 730+ closed computation routes —
constrains *computing* π(x) from scratch. None of it constrains
*checking* a claimed value produced by a prover who did the work. That
asymmetry is real and exploitable:

> **Protocol (S491).** An untrusted prover who runs the Lucy_Hedgehog
> sieve DP can convince a verifier of the EXACT value of π(x) with
> unconditional (information-theoretic) soundness — no hardness
> assumptions, no trusted setup. The verifier checks each of the
> K = π(√x) sieve layers by a degree-≤3 sum-check and never touches
> any Θ(x)-size object. Verifier cost: Õ(n·Σ_{p≤√x} p) field ops with
> automaton wiring (designed improvement to Õ(√x) via carry-chain
> wiring); communication Õ(K·n); soundness error ≤ ~7nK/q.

Measured (q = 2³¹−1): π(65535) = 6542, π(262143) = 23000,
π(1048575) = 82025 all verified exactly; verifier 69 ms → 0.9 s while
x grows 16×; transcripts 28–110 KB; **50/50 cheating provers rejected**,
including self-consistent liars that corrupt one DP entry and recompute
all downstream layers coherently.

## The two structural observations that make it work

1. **The sieve recursion is made of small-automaton predicates.** The
   verifier's bottleneck in any sum-check is evaluating the multilinear
   extension (MLE) of the summand at a random field point. The MLE of
   the *primality indicator* is dense — 0.71 nonzero-coefficient
   fraction, 2^{n/2} coefficients (S48 / E2.1) — which is precisely why
   sum-check-for-computing-π(x) died at S18/S48. But the Lucy recurrence
   `S_i(v) = S_{i−1}(v) − [v ≥ p_i²]·(S_{i−1}(⌊v/p_i⌋) − (i−1))`
   contains no primality predicate: floor-division ⌊v/p⌋ is a p-state
   long-division automaton, the threshold [v ≥ p²] a 3-state comparator,
   and any width-W bit-automaton predicate has an MLE evaluable at an
   arbitrary point in O(n·W) by a transfer-matrix DP. **The sieve is
   verification-friendly because it decomposes primality into automaton
   steps; primality as a monolithic predicate is not.** This is a new
   counterpoint to E2.1: the same density wall that blocks computing
   blocks nothing once the predicate is factored through the recursion.
2. **The Lucy correction scalar is public.** S_{i−1}(p_i − 1) = i − 1
   (the primes below p_i), so each layer needs no extra prover claim
   for its correction term — the layer reductions chain with only two
   point-claims (merged by line restriction) and terminate in the
   closed form S̃_0(z) = Int(z) − 1 + Π(1−z_j).

## Corollaries

- **Succinct certificates for p(n).** "p(n) = y" is certified by (i) an
  ECPP/Pratt primality certificate for y, plus (ii) this protocol run
  on π(y) = n. Kilobyte-scale, unconditionally sound up to the field
  soundness error. Today's trust mechanism for record π(x) values is
  independent recomputation by a different algorithm; this replaces
  months of recomputation with a transcript.
- **Certified comparisons in the hard zone.** The decision problem
  [p(n) ≤ x?] ⟺ [π(x) ≥ n?] is worst-case as hard as computing p(n)
  (binary search, E6.6), and inside the √x-wide hard window around
  R⁻¹(n) each comparison costs a full π(x) computation. But it is
  cheaply *verifiable*: a prover can certify each comparison bit.
  Empirical geography of the decision problem measured in
  `experiments/analytic/guess_comparison_oracle/`: against the biased
  guess li⁻¹(n) the comparison bit is constant (30/30, the
  Rubinstein–Sarnak bias, predictable up to the Skewes scale ~10³¹⁶);
  against the centered guess R⁻¹(n) it is an empirical coin flip
  (10/30 vs 20/30) — the better the guess, the closer the bit is to
  fair, which is the information barrier restated.
- **The verification-complexity landscape (corrected S491-late).** In
  principle, GKR 2008 over the data-parallel uniform primality circuit
  (Σ over w ≤ x of an AKS copy — polylog depth, log-space uniform)
  already gives an unconditionally-sound interactive proof with polylog
  verifier and poly(x) prover — a literature corollary, NOT novel, and
  with astronomically large polylog constants and a nontrivial
  wiring-uniformity verification. (An earlier draft of this file
  posed "polylog or √x floor?" as open; the in-principle answer is
  polylog, by GKR.) The honest open questions are: (a) a *practical*
  polylog-verifier protocol — the S491 Lucy protocol runs in
  milliseconds but its wiring totals Õ(x/log x); **the delegated-wiring
  upgrade (built and measured S491-late,
  `lucy_dp_delegated_wiring.py`) reaches Õ(√x)**: the division
  automaton's DP is itself GKR-delegated, the verifier evaluating the
  transition relation s′ = 2s + a − b·p via a width-4 carry automaton
  in O(log p) — measured 3.2× verifier growth over an 84× p-range (vs
  34× for the automaton baseline, whose linear-in-p cost the
  width-dichotomy theorem proves unavoidable without delegation);
  crossover at p ≈ 130. The remaining √x → polylog gap is now exactly
  the K = π(√x) sequential layer structure of the sieve itself;
  (b) succinct *non-interactive* certificates unconditionally — made
  precise (S491-late): a polylog-size unconditionally-checkable
  certificate for π(x) = c is exactly the statement
  **L_π = {(x, c) : π(x) = c} ∈ NP** in input length n = log x.
  No construction is known (even the "≥ c" direction lacks a succinct
  witness — listing primes costs ~x bits; Pratt/ECPP certify one
  prime, not a count), and no barrier either: for #P-complete
  functions, value-certificates in NP would force NP = coNP, but π(x)
  is not known #P-hard (proving THAT would itself be a major result,
  and is a cleaner formal target than the algorithmic question).
  L_π ∈ NP is the proof-theoretic shadow of the headline problem:
  polylog computation would trivially imply polylog certificates, so
  certificate lower bounds are the easier-to-attack face of the same
  wall; (c) the constructibility dichotomy below.

## The width spectrum (S491 brainstorm follow-up, measured)

`experiments/constructions/automaton_width_dichotomy/` upgrades the
project's OBDD-width edge from a computation lower bound to an exact
verification-cost measure: given an explicit read-once branching
program with cut-widths (W_j), the MLE is evaluable at any field point
in O(Σ_j W_j) (transfer DP — Theorem T1, implemented). Measured at
x = 2²⁴ with matched-random control:

- **Division wiring [u = ⌊v/p⌋] has Nerode width exactly 2p+1** —
  the S491 protocol's O(n·p) wiring check is optimal among explicit
  automatons; prover-supplied carry witnesses are *necessary* (not just
  sufficient) to go below.
- **χ_P's width profile = incompressible plateau + admissibility
  cliff**: W_j = 2^j exactly through j = 16 (every aligned 256-window
  of primes distinct — the global pseudorandom side), then a crash to
  44× below random (107 vs 4707 distinct aligned 16-windows — wheel/HL
  local rigidity made quantitative). The cut-profile invariant
  D_k(x) = #distinct aligned k-windows of χ_P is new to the project
  and bridges its global-randomness and local-structure edge families
  in one curve.
- **Middle-cut width is maximal (2^{n/2} = 4096 > E2.1 rank 2050)** —
  refines the rank edge: the factor-2 deficiency is linear-algebraic,
  not informational.
- **One-shot sum-check verification of π(x) is dead twice over**:
  Σ_j W_j(χ_P) ~ x^c with c drifting 0.73 → 0.77 upward (peak-crossover
  argument gives c → 1), AND the minimal program is non-constructible
  without the primes. Verification must consume primality through
  explicit small-width sieve predicates — layering is structurally
  forced, which is exactly what the Lucy protocol does.
- **The cliff is exactly Hardy-Littlewood (S491 continuation,
  `experiments/analytic/local_pattern_census/`).** W_j = D_k(2ⁿ)
  (k = 2^{n−j}) by definition, and the census saturates at
  **D_k(x) = A_k + 1** — the exactly-enumerable count of HL-admissible
  aligned patterns, plus the single m = 0 window containing the small
  primes. Verified to closure: k = 8 (14 = 13+1), k = 16 (107 = 106+1,
  all admissible realized by x = 2¹⁸, stable through 2²⁸); k = 32
  converging (3385 of A₃₂+1 = 3574 at 2²⁶; the 189 missing are exactly
  the weight ≥ 6 dense constellations — the census deficit is a
  finite-x probe of k-tuple uniformity). Max weights 3/5/9 match the
  classical H(k) narrowest-tuple function. **The prime indicator's
  width spectrum = global-pseudorandom plateau + admissible-pattern
  entropy curve**, with the crossover set by the (open) entropy
  constant lim log₂(A_k)/k (measured 0.46 → 0.37 at k = 8 → 32).

## Honest scope

- No speedup for computing π(x); the prover pays the full sieve cost.
  This is an adjacent-problem partial-positive in the S224 mold —
  computation unchanged, trust exponentially cheaper.
- The protocol composes standard tools (LFKN 1992 sum-check; GKR-style
  layer reductions; CMT 2012 prover techniques). The novelty is the
  application target (no prior verification protocol for π(x) exists),
  the automaton-MLE treatment of the sieve wiring, and the public-
  scalar observation that makes the Lucy chain close without auxiliary
  claims.
- Demo field q = 2³¹−1 (soundness ~10⁻⁶ at n=16). **Field lift (S498,
  corrected):** the multiply-trace identity U·a+R−X=0 is sound only while
  the field's CHARACTERISTIC exceeds the integers it relates (U·a ~ x),
  i.e. q > x, roughly n ≲ 30. The lift is therefore to a larger-
  characteristic PRIME (q ~ 2⁶¹−1 for n ≲ 60, generic ~128-bit prime for
  cryptographic x) — NOT an extension field. An extension field F_{q²} has
  q² *elements* but characteristic q, so an aliasing forgery (off by k·q)
  embeds as the SAME field element as the truth and is undetectable; the
  larger element count only shrinks Schwartz–Zippel error, an orthogonal
  concern. Demonstrated end-to-end in `compressed_prover_mult_trace.py`
  (`--field`, `--alias-demo`, `--refute-q2`). The genuine alternative to a
  bigger prime is a small-field schoolbook carry trace. **The lift is now
  threaded through the WHOLE compressed chain (S499):** `compressed_layer.py`
  `run_chain` and the delegated wiring (`lucy_dp_delegated_wiring.py`) carry a
  prime-modulus `q` (`--field {q,big,small}`), default `q=2³¹−1` bit-identical,
  `q=2⁶¹−1` over exact-int object arrays — the chain over `big` gives
  `claimed π==sieve` with all cheats rejected, and the wrap-around alias the demo
  prime admits is rejected by the lift in the chain's exact trace config. The
  remaining gap to a large-n run is speed, not soundness — but (**S500**) the
  obvious speed fix is not the bottleneck: the numpy `2⁶¹−1` mulmod
  (`_mul61`/`_sum61`, `2⁶¹≡1` fold) is built and threaded chain-wide
  bit-identically, yet it is a *large-array-only* win (the single-`√x`-cube
  certifier gains 1.7–3.8× at n=24–28; the **full chain is slower**, being
  `π(√x)` layers of many small cubes — *operation-count-bound*, not
  width-bound). The pure-Python Lucy DP is also negligible (`<0.1%` of
  `run_chain`). So the real lever for a fast large-x chain run is reducing the
  *count* of small per-layer field-ops (cross-cube batching), kept opt-in
  (`--fast-big`) with BIG_Q on the object reference by default.
  Demo prover is table-based Θ(2ⁿ/layer); production prover works the O(√x)
  compressed Lucy state at Õ(x) total.
- **Leaf openings (S505).** Each layer's claim is grounded by opening a committed
  O(√x)-size MLE at a point. The demo closed these by direct `mle_eval`
  (O(√x) each → O(K·√x) ≈ Õ(x) over the chain, the last √x-/p-linear verifier
  term). `leaf_open.py` builds the standard **sum-check opening** — `S~(pt)=Σ_w
  S[w]eq~(pt,w)` is itself a degree-2 sum-check — reducing an opening at `pt` to a
  polylog transcript (verifier O(nb)) plus ONE residual claim at a fresh point.
  `run_chain(--pcs)` threads each fold's residual as the next layer's carried
  claim, discharged transitively at the S₀ base — **unconditional** (no
  commitment; soundness rides the GKR layer reductions). Measured: the standalone
  opening verifier is flat in 2^nb (6.5×→432× over `mle_eval` as nb grows;
  21×→3605× over BIG_Q); the chain integration is a **stable ~1.2–1.36× verifier
  win**, NOT yet asymptotic — the remaining per-layer O(2^nb) term is the trace
  region's nb Ub-bit-table openings (per-layer witness data, no carried claim to
  thread to), which want the batched-trace integration. A real multilinear
  commitment (Brakedown/FRI-free) would discharge all residuals succinctly under a
  hashing assumption, trading unconditionality for full succinctness.
- **Batched Ub openings (S506) — the per-layer verifier is now leaf-eval-free.**
  That one remaining per-layer O(2^nb) term is closed. The nb Ub-bit-table openings
  `Ub_{Lv−nb+k}~(r_C)` (the B2 routing that pins g1_trace to the certified quotient
  u_e) are EXACTLY the tables the batched trace zero-test (`batched_trace`,
  `verify_constraints_batched`) already stacks and commits along the layer axis, so
  the discharge SHARES that commitment. Each layer defers `(l, r_C^l, [ub_{l,k}])`
  (the prover supplies the scalars; the verifier folds them into B2's `expect` in
  O(nb)) and all K·nb discharge in **ONE degree-2 sum-check**: with γ←F_q, β=γ^nb the
  weight β^l·γ^k=γ^{l·nb+k} is a distinct power, and the identity factorizes to a
  single inner product `Σ_w B[w]·C[w]` over the (Lk+nb)-cube — B the verifier-anchored
  per-layer eq weights (the soundness anchor, recomputed in O(K(Lk+nb))), C the γ-fold
  of the committed low-nb Ub tables (its opening taken from the sum-check's folded
  scalar, exactly as the zero-test trusts its bit scalars). `verify_ub_openings_batched`;
  wired behind `run_chain(--pcs --batch_trace --batch_ub)`. **Measured: the verifier-
  side O(2^nb) Ub-leaf eval count drops K·nb→0 at every n** (moved to the prover); the
  per-layer verifier is leaf-eval-free, so the only O(√x) verifier work left is
  one-time — the two S₀ base closes plus the batched discharges. **The unconditional
  Õ(√x) end-to-end verifier is now structurally real.** Honest scope: the wall-clock
  t_verifier win is a modest ~1.1–1.2× and flat in n (a vectorised numpy `mle_eval`
  over a √x-size array is cheap relative to the Python-loop wiring/eq recomputes that
  dominate the measured t_verifier), so the asymptotic O(K·nb·2^nb)→one-time gain is in
  **op-count, not measured wall-clock** at reachable n — correcting the S505 prediction
  that the verifier ratio would grow with n. Only a real outer commitment for the two
  one-time S₀ base closes remains (computational, not unconditional).
- **Tensor polynomial commitment for the base closes (S508) — the whole-chain
  verifier is now sub-√x.** That last one-time term is closed. `pcs_commit.py` is a
  hash-based multilinear PCS (Ligero/Brakedown tensor style): reshape the 2^nb table
  into an r×k matrix (r=2^{n1}, k=2^{n2}, n1+n2=nb), RS-encode each row, Merkle-commit
  the N columns (sha256 = CRH/RO stand-in). Using `eq~(pt,w)=eq~(pt_hi,w_hi)·eq~(pt_lo,
  w_lo)` so `S~(pt)=a^T M b` (a=eq_table(pt_hi), b=eq_table(pt_lo)), the **evaluation-
  proof verifier is O(t·(r+k)) = O(x^{1/4}·polylog)** — sub-√x: it reads the two
  combined messages v=a^T M, w=ρ^T M (len k), checks the eval binding ⟨v,b⟩=claimed,
  and at t Fiat–Shamir columns checks Merkle membership + the linear-code consistency
  Enc(v)[c]=⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩, Enc(w)[c]=⟨ρ,Mhat[:,c]⟩. The full 2^nb table never touches
  the verifier. Wired behind `run_chain(--commit-base)`; with `--pcs --batch_trace
  --batch_ub --commit-base` the **whole-chain verifier is sub-√x**. Measured
  (`--bench-verifier-ops`, config d): leading-term exponent **α_ops = 0.258 ≈ 0.25
